short_description: Vitiligo is a skin condition where patches of skin lose pigment and become lighter or white. It is not contagious, but it can spread over time and may need dermatology follow-up.
common_symptoms: patches on face, hands, arms, or body
sometimes white hair in affected areas
temporary_advice: Protect affected areas from sun exposure
Avoid skin trauma or harsh products
Consider dermatology advice for treatment options
avoid: Avoid strong sun exposure without protection
Do not use random bleaching or whitening products
Avoid scratching or irritating the skin
Do not assume it is contagious
risk_notes: Vitiligo is not contagious and is usually not dangerous, but it can spread and affect confidence. Sun protection is important because lighter patches burn more easily.
when_to_see_doctor: If patches are on face, hands, or sensitive areas
